caption:
Dead hangs are all over Lulu's feed. Are they actually good for your shoulders?

For many people, hanging from a bar is a handy way to build grip strength and get used to having the arms overhead. Research on hangs specifically is limited, though, so treat them as one useful tool rather than a shoulder reset.

Start with your toes on a box so your legs take some weight, hang for 10 to 20 seconds for a few sets, and build time over several weeks. Mix passive hangs with active ones where you draw the shoulder blades down. Lingering pain, a recent dislocation or tingling into the hand are reasons to get assessed first.

Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.
